reading.body:
Qualcomm's public record shows a company filing quarterly results and current reports on a steady cadence, with no disclosed litigation or regulatory cases attached to it. The eight SEC filings span March to September 2026, including two 10-Qs and six 8-Ks, which is the ordinary rhythm of a large public reporting company rather than a signal of distress or expansion.

The profile places Qualcomm in San Diego and describes it as designing mobile processors, AI chips, and wireless technology, with essential patents in 5G and earlier mobile standards. That is the extent of what the data supports about its AI position. There is no revenue figure, no data center count, no power contract, and no customer named here, so nothing in this record shows how much of Qualcomm's business is AI compute or where that compute physically runs.

The one geographic fact with legal weight is California, listed with a count of 281. The data does not say what that count measures, so it cannot be read as lawsuits, violations, or exposure of any specific kind. It does establish that Qualcomm's regulatory and legal footprint sits in the same state as its headquarters.

What this record does not cover is the part that matters most for the compute thesis. It contains no fab, no building, no megawatt, and no grid interconnection. Qualcomm designs chips rather than operating the power and shell that constrain AI scaling, and nothing in these filings contradicts or confirms that distinction.

profile_text.body:
Qualcomm is a technology company headquartered in San Diego, California. It designs mobile processors, AI chips and wireless technology, and holds essential patents in the 5G, 4G, CDMA2000, TD-SCDMA and WCDMA mobile standards.

Source: Wikipedia, Qualcomm, retrieved 22 September 2026.
